facts.text: Founded in 1875 as a Methodist campground, Thousand Island Park evolved into a family retreat with a Chautauqua‑style mix of religion, culture, and recreation.
In 1982, Thousand Island Park earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places, safeguarding its distinctive cottage architecture for future generations.
The Landmark Society, born in 1976 after the park’s Centennial Celebration, now stewards the historic district’s character and integrity.
Every summer, volunteers host Craftsman/Bungalow cottage workshops, teaching residents how to preserve the park’s unique architectural styles.
Vivekananda Cottage, a Hindu sacred site, attracts visitors who followed Swami Vivekananda and his followers to the park.
Just 0.5 miles southeast lies Rock Island Light, a historic lighthouse perched in the middle of the St. Lawrence River’s south channel.
